messages:
maria: Quick question — onboarding a customer that needs full telemetry off (UA, client metrics, tracing) for streaming usage. What's the minimal set of flags/envs to disable in Python and Node SDKs? Also any streaming handshake gotchas for headers/tracing? 

aj: @maria short answer: set telemetry off at client init + env var. Details: 

- Node: pass { enableTelemetry: false } to RedwoodClient (or process.env.REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY = "1")
- Python: RedwoodClient(..., enable_telemetry=False) or export REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1

Remember to remove/override User-Agent header in requests if they want zero UA. Example Node override:

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ enableTelemetry: false, headers: { 'user-agent': '' } })
```

kai: small caveat: for streaming (chunked HTTP / SSE / websockets) headers are only sent at handshake. If their proxy strips headers after handshake, tracing won't propagate. Recommend using a stable trace header like `x-redwood-trace` or the standard `traceparent` (W3C) and ensure proxies forward it.

maria: got it — what about the metrics pipeline? If they disable metrics client-side do we still get server-side runtime metrics? 

aj: yes server-side platform metrics remain (infra, latency, tokens) unless they opt out at tenant level. Client metric toggles only stop SDK telemetry (client-side counters, SDK versions, user-agent). 

kai: also note race: if you set env var AFTER importing the SDK it may be too late for some wrappers. Recommend set env vars before process start or pass flags at init. 

ci-bot: Reminder: doc PR needed — add a short snippet to SDK quickstart for telemetry opt-out. https://git.internal/redwood/devex/sdk-docs/pull/782 :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — I'll file the PR and ping for review. :raised_hands:
